entries.title: Stuck at the Claude sign-in terminal window
entries.sub: The black window is the sign-in — here is exactly what to press
symptoms: what do I do with the terminal
steps: The black window IS the sign-in. The Claude desktop app is a separate product and does not connect the Trade Companion.

Version 0.3.18 and later: the window sends you straight to your browser. Sign in to claude.ai with the account that has your subscription and click Authorize. The window then says "Login successful". Close it and the light turns green by itself.

Browser did not open? The window prints a link: select it, right-click to copy, and paste it into your browser. After you authorize, the page shows a code with a # in the middle. Copy ALL of it, both halves, then right-click in the black window to paste it at "Paste code here if prompted >" and press Enter. A code works once and expires in a few minutes, so if it says "Invalid code", close the window and start again from the Claude light.

Version 0.3.17 and earlier: if it asks you to choose a text style or theme, press Enter. If it asks "Do you trust this folder?", press Enter on "Yes". On a sign-in wizard, choose "Claude account with subscription". On a normal prompt (or "Welcome back!"), type /login, press Enter, and choose "Claude account with subscription".

If the window says "Welcome back!" and the bottom line reads "401 Missing Authentication Header - Retrying", the very first run picked the Anthropic Console (API billing) option. Your subscription is fine: press Esc once, type /login, press Enter, and choose "Claude account with subscription".
Make sure the browser is signed into claude.ai with the same account as your subscription.

entries.title: The Claude sign-in window closes instantly, or says it can't connect
entries.sub: This one is your internet path to Anthropic — not the app, not your subscription
symptoms: unable to connect to anthropic services
please check your internet connection and network settings
steps: First: the window is no longer allowed to vanish. On current versions it stays open and prints the reason, and that message is the whole diagnosis — read it before changing anything.

If it says "Unable to connect to Anthropic services" or "Failed to connect to platform.claude.com", nothing is wrong with the app, your install, or your Claude subscription. Your computer could not open a connection to Anthropic, so the sign-in had nothing to talk to.

Fastest way to split the problem in one move: turn on your phone's hotspot, connect this computer to it, and run the sign-in again. If it works on the hotspot, the block is in your normal network — router, ISP, DNS filtering, or a VPN — not on this computer.

If the hotspot fails too, it is something on the computer. The usual culprit is a security suite that inspects HTTPS traffic (Avast, AVG, Bitdefender, Kaspersky, ESET, Norton). Turn its web shield / HTTPS scanning off temporarily, retry the sign-in, then turn it back on once you are signed in.
Turn off any VPN and retry. Work, school, and guest networks block this often too — if you are on one, try a home network.
Windows Firewall can also block it: allow claude.exe (in the app's folder, under resources) through the firewall, or retry with the firewall briefly off on a network you trust.
Still stuck after the hotspot test? Send the exact text from that window to tyler@thepurposedriventrader.com — that message names the real cause and is the fastest thing to act on.

entries.title: "Connection port live" stays red
entries.sub: TradingView must be started by the app — not from its own shortcut
steps: This light is about TradingView, not Claude — TradingView must be STARTED BY THE APP so the two can talk.
Close TradingView completely (check the system tray — right-click the TradingView icon and quit).
Press the button below (or "Launch TradingView" in the sidebar).
The light goes green within seconds of TradingView finishing its load.
Every time you restart TradingView, launch it from the app again — a normally-started TradingView can never connect.

Launch works but the port light STILL stays red? Something else on this computer may be using the connection port TradingView needs. Close other tools that use browser automation or "remote debugging" (other trading bots, screen-automation apps, a browser started with a debugging flag), then click Launch again — the app now tells you if it finds one.

On Windows 10, if Launch keeps timing out after 30 seconds: close TradingView completely (check the system tray), wait ten seconds, then click Launch once more. Still stuck? Use the ? menu → Troubleshoot → "Email me" — your report now carries exactly how the last launch ended.

entries.title: "TradingView running" is red
entries.sub: TradingView Desktop is not open yet
steps: TradingView Desktop isn't open. The button below starts it the connected way.
No TradingView Desktop installed yet? Download it free from tradingview.com/desktop, install, then come back and use the button below (not the desktop shortcut).

entries.title: "Engine installed" is red
entries.sub: Part of the install is missing: an antivirus quarantine, or an update that was interrupted
steps: Part of the app's install is missing. The two usual causes are an antivirus quarantine, and an automatic update that was interrupted while the app's helper was still running. If "Node runtime" is red too, it is almost always the update.
Close the Trade Companion completely (check the system tray too), then reinstall from desk.thepurposedriventrader.com/download. The installer goes over the top and keeps your chats and settings.
If it goes red again later, open Windows Security, then Protection history, and restore anything quarantined from the tv-command-hub folder. Tell me which antivirus you use.
Version 0.3.18 and later stop the helper before an update installs, so an update can no longer leave it half-removed.
Still red after a reinstall? Use "Report to PDT" on any failed tool in chat so the details reach the developer.

entries.title: "Could not start TradingView: spawn EPERM"
entries.sub: Windows blocked the launch — one paste fixes it
steps: TradingView now ships for Windows as a Microsoft Store style package, which installs into a protected folder. On some machines Windows refuses to let the app start it, and the Launch button fails with "spawn EPERM" — or TradingView simply closes and never comes back.
The fix: close TradingView completely, open PowerShell (press the Windows key, type "powershell", Enter), and paste this one line:
irm https://desk.thepurposedriventrader.com/launch-tv.ps1 | iex

That runs our small launch helper — it starts TradingView the way Windows wants, with the connection port open, and tells you in plain words when it has connected. (Cautious? Open the link in your browser first and read it — it is short.)
When it says "Connected", open the Trade Companion: both "TradingView running" and "Connection port live" should be green. You can skip the Launch button and start TradingView this way any time.
Also make sure you are on the latest app version (the ? menu shows it) — newer releases handle more of these machines automatically, and updates install themselves.
Starting TradingView from its normal shortcut will NOT work — that opens it without the connection port, which is why the port light stays red even though TradingView is clearly running.

entries.title: Everything is green but chat replies with an error
entries.sub: Expired sign-ins and plan limits look like app problems — they aren't
symptoms: not logged in error in chat
steps: Click the Claude status light even if it looks connected — if it's yellow, your sign-in expired: run the sign-in again (terminal → /login → Claude account with subscription).
If chat mentions usage limits, your Claude plan hit its cap — it resets on Claude's schedule; the app itself is fine.
If a specific tool keeps failing, click "Report to PDT" on the failed tool — the report carries the technical details automatically.

entries.title: Cancelling or managing your Claude subscription
entries.sub: This app never bills you — your Claude plan lives with Anthropic
steps: The Trade Companion is free and never charges you. The copilot runs on YOUR Claude account, so any Claude charge comes from Anthropic (or the App Store / Google Play if you subscribed on your phone) — not from this app.
Subscribed on the web: claude.ai → your profile → Settings → Billing → Cancel plan.
Subscribed in the Claude phone app (the usual reason it does not appear under Billing on the website): cancel in the App Store → Subscriptions, or Google Play → Payments & subscriptions.
Using an API key from platform.claude.com instead: nothing renews — it is pay-as-you-go and stops when the balance runs out.
After cancelling, the copilot stops working (no Claude account to run on), but the app stays installed and costs nothing; sign in again any time to resume.

entries.title: Chat says Claude’s runtime crashed (Snapdragon / ARM laptops)
entries.sub: A Windows-on-ARM laptop running an Intel-only program — your install is fine
steps: If your laptop has a Snapdragon processor (most Copilot+ PCs, the ARM Surface Laptop), this is a known crash and it is not your install, your sign-in, or your subscription — nothing you reinstall will change it.
Claude’s own program ships only as an Intel build, so Windows translates it while it runs. That translation layer is where it dies, mid-answer.

The app already resends your message automatically when this happens, and the resend usually goes through. When it still fails, send the same message once more by hand — in the reports we have, the hand-resend succeeds about half the time within two minutes.
If it crashes several times in a row, close and reopen the app once, then resend. A fresh run clears whatever state the emulator was in.
Your chat history is never lost to this crash, and no trade data is affected.

Please click "Report to PDT" when it happens: those reports are how we are tracking a native ARM build. Mention "Snapdragon" in an email to tyler@thepurposedriventrader.com if you want to be told when it ships.

entries.title: Chat says your Claude sign-in moved to the vault or was emptied out
entries.sub: Another Claude Code install on this PC changed the sign-in the app was sharing. One sign-in through the app fixes it
symptoms: already signed in but light is yellow
light is green but chat says sign in
claude code works but the app says connect
welcome back but not logged in
says I am already logged in
signed in yesterday now it asks again
steps: This happens when Claude Code is also installed on the PC on its own. It moves the sign-in the two were sharing into the Windows credential vault, or replaces it with its own, and the copy of Claude inside the Trade Companion is left with an empty one. Nothing is wrong with your subscription.

Version 0.3.18 or later (Settings shows the version): click the yellow Claude light at the top of the sidebar, then "Open the Claude sign-in window". Your browser opens to claude.ai: sign in and click Authorize. The window says "Login successful" and the light turns green. From then on the app keeps its own sign-in, separate from other Claude installs.

Version 0.3.17, where the light can stay green: press Windows key + R, paste this line, and press Enter: "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\tv-command-hub\resources\app.asar.unpacked\node_modules\@anthropic-ai\claude-agent-sdk-win32-x64\claude.exe" auth login . Approve in the browser that opens; the window closes by itself when it is done. Then resend your message.
An Anthropic API key in Settings also works and skips the sign-in entirely.
The app updates itself: it checks on every launch and installs the update when you close it.

entries.title: Chat stops after many steps ("maximum number of turns")
entries.sub: The app’s own per-message safety stop, not a Claude limit. Say "continue" and it picks up where it left off
symptoms: have to tell it to continue
steps: The app lets Claude take a set number of steps (tool calls) on one message: 100 up to version 0.3.17, 200 from 0.3.18. A long job, such as checking an indicator across several timeframes and tickers, can use them all, and the run pauses. Nothing is wrong with your account, your subscription, or the script.
Send "continue". Claude keeps its full memory of the run and gets a fresh set of steps. Everything it built so far is still in the editor and on the chart.
For very long jobs, a few messages of a few parts each also give you results along the way.
The cap exists on purpose: every step spends your own Claude usage, and the cap is what stops a stuck loop from running up a bill unattended.
